title: DBQ & LEQ writing
examples: How do I make sure my thesis statement is specific enough?
What is the difference between using context and making a claim?
When should I introduce the source's perspective in my essay?

explain.say: Today we learn about writing strong historical arguments.
First we need a clear thesis statement for your essay.

items: It must be an argument, not a fact.
It guides your entire essay's focus.

explain.say: Next we must analyze the source's perspective using sourcing.

items: Row 2: Who wrote it? | Author's background
Row 3: Why was it written? | Purpose or bias
Row 4: When was it written? | Historical moment

explain.say: Then we set the scene with contextualization for deeper understanding.

items: When: Before the event | What: Broad historical background
When: During the event | What: Immediate causes
When: After the event | What: Long-term impact

explain.say: For example, if studying the American Civil War, your context would cover slavery's history.

draw.text: Example: Slavery's history leads to war

explain.say: In real life, think about a modern news report on climate change.

draw.text: Real Life: News report on climate change

faq.q: How long should my thesis statement be?
faq.a: It should be one focused, clear sentence. Do you need to include evidence in it? You do not need to include evidence in the thesis itself.
asks: Should my thesis be a full paragraph?
Is one sentence enough for my main argument?

faq.q: If I use context, do I have to mention the source's author?
faq.a: No, context helps the reader understand the time period. You must still analyze the source's perspective separately.
asks: Does context replace my analysis of the source?
Can I use context without mentioning the source?

faq.q: Is it okay if my thesis changes during the essay?
faq.a: No, your thesis must remain consistent throughout the entire essay. It is the promise you make to the reader.
asks: Can I argue different things in different paragraphs?
Does my argument have to be the same from start to finish?

faq.q: What is the main difference between sourcing and context?
faq.a: Context sets the background time and place. Sourcing focuses on the source itself: who wrote it and why.
asks: Should I talk about the time or the writer more?

faq.q: When should I write my thesis statement?
faq.a: You should write a working thesis statement before you start writing the body paragraphs. It helps keep your focus sharp.
asks: Do I write this first or last?
Can I write it when I finish the essay?

facts: A thesis statement presents the main argument of the essay.
Sourcing involves questioning the author's perspective and purpose.
Contextualization places the source within its broader historical setting.
A strong thesis must be debatable, not just a statement of fact.

quiz.say: The main argument that guides the entire essay is called the:
quiz.why: The thesis statement is the core argument you are trying to prove to the reader.

wrong.0: Evidence is the proof you use, but it is not the main argument itself.
wrong.2: Sourcing only looks at who wrote the document, not the overall argument.
wrong.3: Contextualization only provides background information about the time period.

quiz.say: Analyzing the author's potential bias or purpose is an example of:
quiz.why: Sourcing requires you to analyze the source itself, including its creator's viewpoint.

wrong.0: Context is about the time period surrounding the source, not the source's intent.
wrong.1: The conclusion summarizes, it does not analyze the source's creation.
wrong.3: The thesis is your argument, not an analysis of the source's creator.

quiz.say: Providing the broad social and political background for an event is called:
quiz.why: Contextualization sets the scene, explaining the 'before' and 'after' of the event.

wrong.0: Sourcing focuses narrowly on the document itself, not the whole era.
wrong.1: Analysis is the skill, but contextualization is the specific technique for background setting.
wrong.3: The thesis is your specific argument about the event, not the background.
